title: Lock after time in the background
summary: Model AppState transitions and lock the app after a background timeout.
prompt: Write `lockReducer(state, event)` with state `{ appState, backgroundedAt, locked }` and events `{ type: 'change', next, at }` (next is `active`, `inactive` or `background`, `at` is a timestamp in ms from an injected clock) and `{ type: 'unlock' }`. Pass the timeout as `createLockReducer(timeoutMs)`. Rules: when entering `background` from any other state, record `backgroundedAt = at` (keep the earliest time if already set). `inactive` alone never records or locks. When becoming `active`, lock if `backgroundedAt` is set and `at - backgroundedAt >= timeoutMs`, then clear `backgroundedAt`. `unlock` clears `locked`. Ignore a `change` to the current state (return the same object). There is no React Native runtime here, so this is modelled as plain TypeScript.
hints: Use `??` to keep the first background time.
Only compare times on the transition to `active`.
